source.title: Exact information propagation through fully-connected feed forward neural networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Its title differs from the catalog title; no missing or garbled text is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares initialization schemes and reports classification accuracy after a fixed number of SGD steps, bearing on initialization-related trainability, but it does not measure training error or learning speed directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy comparisons after 10^4 SGD steps. These are not training-error measurements. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares initialization schemes using test accuracy after a fixed training budget and analyzes signal propagation at initialization. Neither measures V4's learning speed or trainable depth directly. Its own results do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experimental conclusion: both proposed initializations outperform He in the reported comparisons, especially for deeper networks, and orthogonal W0 appears most reliable. The authors interpret this as improved trainability, but the reported empirical measure is fixed-budget test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes initialization and proposes parameter-sharing schemes, then compares them with He initialization; it does not reproduce the original studies' training-speed or training-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, width, depth, and initialization scheme; the authors state that GSM and orthogonal W0 perform better at higher width and that orthogonal W0 seems most reliable.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report higher test accuracy with GSM and orthogonal-submatrix initialization than with He initialization after 10^4 SGD steps, especially at greater tested depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial parameter sharing improves fixed-budget test accuracy in fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST and cropped CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: The analysis shows that preserving expected squared signal norms can coexist with increasing input alignment; the proposed orthogonal-submatrix construction provides perfect dynamical isometry at initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Signal-norm preservation alone does not ensure preservation of input distinctions in Gaussian ReLU ensembles; structured initialization can preserve additional propagation properties.

record.peer_reviewed: 33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), as stated in the paper.
record.problems: The reported experiment figures show test accuracy rather than training error or a direct learning-speed measure. Results are averages over instances with 0.95 confidence intervals, but exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper's initialization-distribution and cosine-similarity analyses are not training-error outcomes named by the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels and the stated recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student spurious local minima and the effect of additional student neurons.
Depth-related training error in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initializations.

Learning speed and trainable depth under different initializations; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in very deep tanh networks; training 10,000-layer convolutional networks. Fixed-budget test accuracy and initialization-time propagation properties do not establish these outcomes.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No numerical figure values are recoverable from the supplied text. The theoretical propagation analyses are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows. The paper is not an original source of any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student local minima and changing student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth-related training error, and normalization.

Plain tanh networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights of the same variance in very deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks. The experiments report test accuracy after a fixed training budget, not learning speed or training error directly.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

reader_labels.condition: Fully-connected ReLU networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 across the tested widths and depths
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that both proposed initializations outperform He and show stable results, especially for deeper networks (R1, R2). The measured outcome is test accuracy after a fixed budget, so this supports initialization-related trainability in this setting.
